sections.overview: The Widow Skimmer is a medium-sized dragonfly, about 42–50 millimetres long, found across much of the United States and parts of southern Canada and Mexico.
sections.identification: Broad dark bands cover the wing bases; mature males develop a pale band near the middle of each wing. The male abdomen becomes powdery white with age, while females and young males retain brown-and-yellow markings.
sections.habitat: It is most often seen beside ponds and lakes, but observations also come from slow streams and nearby open ground.
sections.diet: Adults hunt flying insects and may pursue other dragonflies; the available references do not give a detailed account of larval prey.
sections.behavior: Males perch on waterside vegetation and defend territories against other dragonflies; they may also guard females during egg laying.
sections.reproduction: This is an aquatic-breeding dragonfly, but the species accounts reviewed do not give specific egg-laying details or a consistent larval development time.
sections.ecology: Its range extends more broadly across North America than those of L. forensis and L. incesta, two other Libellula described here.
sections.conservation: The range references document occurrence, not a current global population trend or conservation status; none is inferred here.
